entries.title: Acts 12:1
segments: It was at that time that King Herod began to ill-treat some of the members of the Church.

entries.title: Acts 12:2
segments: He had James, the brother of John, beheaded;

entries.title: Acts 12:3
segments: And, when he saw that the Jews were pleased with this, he proceeded to arrest Peter also. (This was during the Festival of the Unleavened Bread.)

entries.title: Acts 12:4
segments: After seizing Peter, Herod put him in prison, and entrusted him to the keeping of four Guards of four soldiers each, intending, after the Passover, to bring him up before the people.

entries.title: Acts 12:5
segments: So Peter was kept in prison, but meanwhile the prayers of the Church were being earnestly offered to God on his behalf.

entries.title: Acts 12:6
segments: Just when Herod was intending to bring him before the people, on that very night Peter was asleep between two soldiers, chained to them both, while there were sentries in front of the door, guarding the prison.

entries.title: Acts 12:7
segments: Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. The angel struck Peter on the side, and roused him with the words: "Get up quickly."

entries.title: Acts 12:8
segments: The chains dropped from his wrists, and then the angel said: "Put on your girdle and sandals." When Peter had done so, the angel added: "Throw your cloak round you and follow me."

entries.title: Acts 12:9
segments: Peter followed him out, not knowing that what was happening under the angel's guidance was real, but thinking that he was seeing a vision.

entries.title: Acts 12:10
segments: Passing the first Guard, and then the second, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened to them of itself; and, when they had passed through that, and had walked along one street, all at once the angel left him.

entries.title: Acts 12:11
segments: Then Peter came to himself and said: "Now I know beyond all doubt that the Lord has sent his angel, and has rescued me from Herod's hands and from all that the Jewish people have been expecting."

entries.title: Acts 12:12
segments: As soon as he realized what had happened, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was also known as Mark, where a number of people were gathered together, praying.

entries.title: Acts 12:13
segments: On his knocking at the door in the gate, a maidservant, named Rhoda, came to answer it.

entries.title: Acts 12:14
segments: She recognized Peter's voice, but in her joy left the gate unopened, and ran in, and told them that Peter was standing outside.

entries.title: Acts 12:15
segments: "You are mad!" they exclaimed. But, when she persisted that it was so, they said: "It must be his spirit!"

entries.title: Acts 12:16
segments: Meanwhile Peter went on knocking, and, when they opened the gate and saw him, they were amazed.

entries.title: Acts 12:17
segments: Peter signed to them with his hand to be silent, and then told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, adding: "Tell James and the Brethren all this." Then he left the house, and went away to another place.

entries.title: Acts 12:18
segments: In the morning there was a great stir among the soldiers-- what could have become of Peter!

entries.title: Acts 12:19
segments: And, when Herod had made further search for him and failed to find him, he closely questioned the Guard, and ordered them away to execution. Then he went down from Judea to stay at Caesarea.

entries.title: Acts 12:20
segments: It happened that Herod was deeply offended with the people of Tyre and Sidon, but they went in a body to him, and, having succeeded in winning over Blastus, the Chamberlain, they begged Herod for a reconciliation, because their country was dependent on the King's for its food-supply.

entries.title: Acts 12:21
segments: On an appointed day Herod, wearing his state-robes, seated himself on his throne, and delivered an oration.

entries.title: Acts 12:22
segments: The people kept shouting: "It is the voice of God, and not of a man!"

entries.title: Acts 12:23
segments: Instantly an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give God the glory; and he was attacked with worms, and died.

entries.title: Acts 12:24
segments: Meanwhile the Lord's Message kept extending, and spreading far and wide.

entries.title: Acts 12:25
segments: When Barnabas and Saul had carried out their mission, they returned to Jerusalem, and took with them John, who was also known as Mark.
